an enclitic particle which is attached to other parts of speech, meaning although, even if, even though, about which Apollonius de synt. p. 265,9 says: ἐναντιότητα ὁ πέρ (ἐπαγγέλλεται) μετ᾿ αὐξήσεως ἐμφαντικήν [the particle περ indicates opposition with emphatic intensification]. Its use is frequent among epic poets, rarer among tragedians: about which it is said in Thes. vol. 6 p. 752.
περ placed after οὐ, but to be referred to the participle that follows.

Thus Hermann for κρατερὸν ὄνθ᾽ ὁμοίως [being strong likewise].

We have spoken about εἴπερ [if indeed] and καίπερ [although] in their own places. περ compounded with adjectives, pronouns, and relative particles intensifies the meaning of the word with which it is joined: see οἷόσπερ [of what sort], ὅσοσπερ [as much as], ὅσπερ [who], ὥσπερ [as], ὡσπερεί [as if].
